Producer review feedback on CG-0MS934XSL00453HF (raised selection feature, currently in_review): when a card raises, the selection highlight does not raise with it. Additionally the raise slider should go to a maximum of 180px with a default of 60px.

Root cause: in HandView.updateSelectionTints(), applySelectionRaise(true) runs BEFORE the tint loop, so on first selection the raise tween starts before the tint overlay exists — the overlay is created at the resting position and is not in the tween targets, so the card raises while the highlight stays behind. Hover pointerover/pointerout also destroy+recreate the overlay, which can orphan it mid-tween.

## Acceptance criteria

1. Regression tests written FIRST (TDD): animated-path first-selection overlay is included in the raise tween targets; hover repaint reuses the overlay in place; reduced-motion first-selection overlay ends at the raised position.
2. The selection highlight overlay always ends at the raised position on first selection (animated and reduced-motion).
3. GymHandPileScene raise slider: RAISE_MAX = 180, RAISE_DEFAULT = 60; reset() restores the default; Controls help text updated.
4. HandView setSelectionLift() API default remains 0 (opt-in) — backward compatible.
5. npm run build succeeds and all HandView + Gym unit tests pass.

# Run `wl doctor upgrade --confirm` in Tableau-Card-Engine

## Why

This project's worklog database is behind the installed `wl` version. Every `wl` invocation prints:

```
Worklog: database at /home/rgardler/projects/Tableau-Card-Engine/.worklog/worklog.db has schemaVersion=8 but the application expects schemaVersion=9. Required columns were repaired automatically. see 'wl doctor upgrade' to list and apply pending migrations
```

Required columns are being patched on every invocation instead of migrated, and the git hooks are stale. Discovered during the 2026-11-04 downtime-dispatcher RCA (the same finding exists across the other worklog roots).

## Pending work (from `wl doctor upgrade --dry-run --json`)

### Schema migrations (3)

- `20260210-add-needsProducerReview` — Add needsProducerReview INTEGER column to workitems (default 0)
- `20260923-add-audit-fingerprint` — Add nullable fingerprint column to audit_results for content-based freshness gate (WL-0MUBVH5S0008NQ9K)
- `20261015-drop-needsProducerReview` — Legacy: Drop needsProducerReview column (reverted — the flag was restored by 20261016-restore-needsProducerReview) **[UNSAFE]**

### Outdated git hooks

- pre-push, post-checkout, post-merge, post-rewrite, worklog-post-pull

## Goal

As a maintainer, I want this project's worklog schema and git hooks fully up to date, so that `wl` stops auto-patching columns on every call and so every worklog hook behaves like the current template.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. `wl doctor upgrade --dry-run --json` afterwards reports `pending: []` and no hook whose `status` is not `up-to-date`.
2. `wl doctor upgrade --confirm` was executed against this project's database and applied the migrations listed above.
3. A plain `wl list --json` invocation no longer prints the `schemaVersion=8 … expects schemaVersion=9` warning.
4. **Data-safety check.** The count of items with `needsProducerReview == true` is identical before and after:
   `wl list --json | jq '[.workItems[] | select(.needsProducerReview == true)] | length'`
   Record both numbers on this item.
5. `wl doctor` reports no new findings attributable to this upgrade (any residual finding is recorded on a follow-up item, not ignored).
6. The before/after `--dry-run --json` output is recorded in a comment on this item.

## Plan

1. Capture the baseline: `wl doctor upgrade --dry-run --json` plus the `needsProducerReview` count → comment on this item.
2. Run `wl doctor upgrade --confirm`.
3. Re-run `--dry-run` (expect nothing pending) and re-check the `needsProducerReview` count (must be unchanged).
4. If the upgrade touched tracked files (`.githooks/`, hook templates), commit them following build → test → commit order.

## Risks & notes

- `--confirm` applies migrations **non-interactively, including UNSAFE ones**. Review the `[UNSAFE]` entries above before running. The database is the runtime source of truth (SQLite); never edit `.worklog/worklog-data.jsonl` and never run `wl import` (destructive).
- If the `needsProducerReview` count changes, STOP, restore, and raise a `bug` against ContextHub's `wl` migration set instead of continuing — the drop/re-add cycle is the suspected cause of the permanent schema-8 oscillation.

## Provenance

Created from the 2026-11-04 overnight zero-dispatch RCA. Pi session `herdr-1793778909-1527089-27004`, log `/home/rgardler/.pi/agent/sessions/--home-rgardler-projects-ContextHub--/2026-11-04T07-55-10-163Z_herdr-1793778909-1527089-27004.jsonl`.

**Unsafe migrations in this sweep:** `20261015-drop-needsProducerReview`

# Restore pre-push test-cache mirroring (`mirror_suite_cache`) in the canonical wl hook template

discovered-from:CG-0MW1VJRY6001FOPT

## Problem statement

The dev-push gate's test-cache mirroring exists only in this repository's
committed `.githooks/pre-push` and in a stale, gitignored local build of the
`worklog` package — never in the canonical `PRE_PUSH_HOOK_CONTENT` template on
`ContextHub` `dev`. The capability therefore survives only until someone
rebuilds `dist` from `dev` or runs `wl doctor upgrade --confirm`, either of which
silently removes it, and the "landed on `dev` ⇒ green cached full-suite entry at
that commit" invariant breaks for every worktree-originated push.

A previous implementation (commit `8f40463d`, merged) restored the function and
the documentation but left the template source untouched; an audit
(2026-11-04) therefore returned **not ready** — AC1 partial, AC2 partial, AC4
unmet. This brief re-scopes the item to the actual remaining work: land the
upstream template change, pin it with tests on both layers, and remove the false
green that is masking the hazard.

## Users

- **AI agents running `/skill:implement`** rely on a `dev` push from a linked
  worktree leaving a green cached full-suite entry the post-push verification can
  read, instead of `missing`.
- **Auditors / audit F3** auto-verify execution-dependent ACs ("full suite
  passes") from that cache entry instead of re-running an 18–21 min suite.
- **Maintainers of any repository consuming the hook template** (`wl init`,
  `wl doctor upgrade`) expect scaffolding and upgrades to deliver the documented
  mirroring behaviour, not to delete it.

Example user stories:

- "As an agent finishing a work tree, when the pre-push gate runs the full suite
  from my linked worktree, I expect the main checkout's
  `run_tests.py --summary --suite all --json` to report that commit green."
- "As a maintainer, when I rebuild the globally linked `wl` from `dev` and run
  `wl doctor upgrade --dry-run`, I expect `pending: []` and every hook
  `up-to-date`, with no repository-local patch keeping the capability alive."

## Context: what `mirror_suite_cache` is

Not a separate suite — it is step 5 of the v3 `pre-push` hook. After the
full-suite gate goes green on a `dev`/`main` push, it copies cache entries the
gate run wrote into the main checkout's `.worklog/cache`.

- Cache location (`~/.pi/agent/skills/test_cache.py:480-503`):
  `<repo>/.worklog/cache` when `.worklog/` exists, else `<git-dir>/test-cache`,
  else `.test-cache`.
- Keys are content-addressed (`cache_key`, line 506): sha256(normalised command
  + `compute_git_state()`, line 222 = HEAD sha + content of every dirty path), so
  an identical key is an identical run and copying a missing key is always safe.
- Why needed: `implement.py finish` pushes from the linked worktree holding the
  pushed commit (`SA-0MVTFMB7K002Y1F3`). A worktree has no `.worklog/`, so the
  run lands in `<git-dir>/test-cache`, invisible to the main checkout, where
  `run_tests.py --summary` and audit F3 read.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **Canonical template carries the capability.** `PRE_PUSH_HOOK_CONTENT` in
   `../ContextHub/src/doctor/hook-upgrade.ts` contains `mirror_suite_cache` (the
   function plus its post-green invocation), and ContextHub's committed
   `.githooks/pre-push` is byte-identical to it. Commit `9771d9c9`
   (`WL-0MW20XXWE00466FP`) is rebased onto `ContextHub` `dev`, builds cleanly and
   is pushed to ContextHub `dev` — **no** repository-local patch in this repo.
2. **No divergence after a global `wl` refresh.** With the refreshed `wl`
   (`cd ../ContextHub && npm run build` on `dev` — the package is npm-linked and
   `dist` is gitignored; `npm link`/`npm i -g` only if the global link is
   absent), running `wl doctor upgrade --confirm` from this repository leaves
   `wl doctor upgrade --dry-run --json` reporting `pending: []` and all five
   hooks `up-to-date`. Because `core.hooksPath = .githooks`, this is byte
   equality between `.githooks/pre-push` and the installed template.
   The refresh gap in `../SorraAgents` `scripts/install_pi.sh` (it wires hooks
   but never refreshes the `wl` it depends on) is recorded as a follow-up work
   item, not fixed here.
3. **Worktree pushes stay visible to the main checkout.** A `dev` push from a
   linked worktree (the `implement.py finish` path) leaves a green full-suite
   cache entry in the **main checkout's** `.worklog/cache` for that exact commit,
   so `run_tests.py --summary --suite all --json` reports a green (not `missing`)
   entry. Re-verify after the template change; the current state is only green
   because of the stale `dist`.
4. **Behaviour is pinned on both layers.** (a) The upstream template test in
   ContextHub (`tests/pre-push-hook-gate.test.ts`, the mirroring + fail-soft
   assertions shipped in `9771d9c9`) passes against the landed template. (b) A
   TCE-side test in `tests/scripts/game-repo-scaffold-hook-gate.test.ts` runs the
   **committed** hook from a linked worktree and asserts a green run's cache entry
   appears in the main checkout's cache with the `mirrored cache entry <name>`
   log line, and that an unmirrorable entry only warns
   (`warning: could not mirror cache entry`) without failing the push.
5. **Documentation attributes the behaviour to the canonical template.**
   `docs/DEVELOPER.md` and the implement skill's dev-push-gate step describe the
   mirroring as template behaviour, and `../ContextHub/docs/migrations.md`
   documents it in the hook section (delivered with `9771d9c9`).
6. **All related documentation is updated** to reflect the changes, including
   code comments, `README`, and any relevant wiki or docs-site entries.
7. **The full project test suite passes** with the new changes (and the changed
   scope passes before each commit).

## Constraints

- The capability must not exist as a repo-local divergence: `wl doctor upgrade`
  must report zero pending changes, so any hook edit lands in the template first.
- The mirror stays **fail-soft**: no copy failure may fail a push, and it never
  overwrites an existing entry.
- `--gate-commit` binding of the gate is **out of scope** (blocked follow-up
  `CG-0MW2151GL003SV5E`); so is the hardened `hook_dir="$(CDPATH= cd -- …)"`
  wrapper form (behaviourally equivalent; recorded on this item's history).
- `install_pi.sh` global-`wl` refresh is out of scope (follow-up item).
- Cross-repo pushes go to each repo's `dev` only, never `main`.

## Existing state (re-verified 2026-11-04T20:25Z, plan session)

- **AC1 is now met upstream.** `9771d9c9` is an ancestor of `ContextHub` `dev`
  (`git merge-base --is-ancestor 9771d9c9 dev` exits 0), and
  `grep -c mirror_suite_cache ../ContextHub/src/doctor/hook-upgrade.ts` returns 2
  (the function plus its post-green invocation). `../ContextHub/.githooks/pre-push`
  is byte-identical to this repo's `.githooks/pre-push` (`diff` clean) — no
  repository-local patch.
- **AC2 is now met (no longer a false green).** The installed `wl` resolves to
  `../ContextHub/dist`, whose `doctor/hook-upgrade.js` was built at 16:03, after
  the landed `src` (15:56); `wl doctor upgrade --dry-run --json` from this repo
  reports `pending: []` and all five hooks `up-to-date`.
- **AC4 is still unmet — the only outstanding capability gap.** The upstream
  template test exists (`../ContextHub/tests/pre-push-hook-gate.test.ts`,
  mirroring + no-overwrite + fail-soft, ~lines 296-408) but
  `tests/scripts/game-repo-scaffold-hook-gate.test.ts` has no mirroring
  assertion ("mirror" appears only in a comment at line 20).
- **AC3 needs re-proof, not new code.** The committed hook still carries
  `mirror_suite_cache` (`.githooks/pre-push:90`, invoked after a green gate at
  :150), but the worktree-push mirroring has not been re-verified since the
  template landed; the item's own `dev` push is the natural evidence.
- **AC5 is met.** `docs/DEVELOPER.md` ("Dev-push gate and test-cache mirroring")
  and the implement skill's dev-push-gate step both attribute the mirroring to
  the canonical `PRE_PUSH_HOOK_CONTENT` template; `9771d9c9` carries
  `../ContextHub/docs/migrations.md`.
- The audit of 2026-11-04 (`rgardler`) returned **not ready** (AC1 *partial*,
  AC2 *partial*, AC4 *unmet*); AC1/AC2 have since been satisfied upstream, so
  the remaining work is AC4(b) plus re-proof of AC3.

## Desired change

Land the upstream template change (rebase, rebuild, test, push to ContextHub
`dev`), refresh the global `wl`, confirm zero hook divergence, add the TCE-side
committed-hook test, and align the documentation — leaving the capability owned
by the canonical template.

## Verification commands (copy-paste ready)

```bash
# AC1/AC2 — land upstream, rebuild the linked wl, prove zero divergence
cd ../ContextHub && git rebase dev wl-WL-0MW20XXWE00466FP-pre-push-cache-mirror
cd ../ContextHub && npm run build
cd ../Tableau-Card-Engine && wl doctor upgrade --confirm
cd ../Tableau-Card-Engine && wl doctor upgrade --dry-run --json   # pending: [], all up-to-date

# AC3 — worktree push leaves a green entry in the main checkout's cache
python3 $(skill_path test)/scripts/run_tests.py --summary --suite all --json   # green at the pushed commit

# AC4 — both layers
cd ../ContextHub && npx vitest run tests/pre-push-hook-gate.test.ts
npx vitest run --project unit tests/scripts/game-repo-scaffold-hook-gate.test.ts
```

## Key Files (predicted)

- `../ContextHub/src/doctor/hook-upgrade.ts` — `PRE_PUSH_HOOK_CONTENT` gains
  `mirror_suite_cache` + its post-green invocation (from `9771d9c9`).
- `../ContextHub/.githooks/pre-push` — committed hook kept byte-identical to the
  template (ContextHub's own doctor self-check enforces this).
- `../ContextHub/tests/pre-push-hook-gate.test.ts` — template behaviour test
  (mirroring + fail-soft), from `9771d9c9`.
- `../ContextHub/docs/migrations.md` — hook-section documentation.
- `tests/scripts/game-repo-scaffold-hook-gate.test.ts` — new TCE-side cases
  against the committed hook (mirror entry + fail-soft warning).
- `docs/DEVELOPER.md` — "Dev-push gate and test-cache mirroring" wording
  confirmed/updated to name the canonical template as the source.
- `skill/implement/SKILL.md` (SorraAgents) — dev-push-gate step wording.
- `.githooks/pre-push` — unchanged (must remain byte-identical to the template).

## Risks & assumptions

- **Latent hazard until AC1 lands**: any `npm run build` in `../ContextHub` on
  `dev` removes the function from the template; the next
  `wl doctor upgrade --confirm` overwrites the committed hook. Mitigation: land
  `9771d9c9` first, then rebuild.
- **Branch may have drifted**: `9771d9c9` was dropped once by a ContextHub `dev`
  reset; the rebase may conflict in `src/doctor/hook-upgrade.ts` and
  `.githooks/pre-push`. Git is the recovery path (the branch retains it).
- **False-green verification**: AC2/AC3 must be checked after a *rebuild from
  `dev`*, not against the current stale `dist`.
- **Each `dev` push runs a full suite** (~18–21 min via the gate), so verification
  cost dominates.
- **Scope-creep risk**: adopting the newest hook wholesale (`--gate-commit`,
  hardened wrappers) is deliberately excluded; record as linked items only.
- Assumption: `WL-0MW20XXWE00466FP` is the ContextHub home for this change, and
  `SA-0MW20Y5YI004QS3M` for the implement-skill wording.
- Assumption: the push transport may need the HTTPS + `gh` credential-helper
  workaround on this host (SSH key not registered on GitHub); no persistent
  config change.
- Assumption: `npm run build` is run on a clean `ContextHub` `dev` checkout; a
  dirty or non-`dev` tree would rebuild the wrong template.
- Assumption: ContextHub keeps its own committed `.githooks/pre-push`
  byte-identical to the template (its doctor self-check compares the two), so
  landing `9771d9c9` must update both.
- Risk: the TCE-side test can pass while the upstream template test fails (and
  vice versa); AC4's two halves must both be reported, never one for the other.

## Plan (2026-11-04, plan skill — stage `plan_complete`)

The remaining work is small (one test file, one verification pass, one
bookkeeping record), so the decomposition is a single vertical phase with no
further phasing: the capability itself already landed upstream, and every AC is
now either met or satisfied by one of the three children below.

Children (test-first order):

1. **Pin pre-push cache mirroring in the committed-hook test** (`CG-0MW2KEFMA000YY66`, task) — AC4(b):
   add the mirror / no-overwrite / fail-soft cases to
   `tests/scripts/game-repo-scaffold-hook-gate.test.ts`, run against the
   **committed** hook. No change to `.githooks/pre-push` (byte-equality with the
   template is a hard constraint).
2. **Verify zero-divergence and worktree cache mirroring end-to-end** (`CG-0MW2KEXFZ0080BP7`, task) —

   --json` → `pending: []`, the item's own worktree `dev` push logging
   `mirrored cache entry …`, and `run_tests.py --summary --suite all --json`

   suite, which must include the new pin).
3. **Record the install_pi.sh global-`wl` refresh gap as a follow-up** (`CG-0MW2KF710003IUEZ`, chore) —

**Coverage-review note.** `apply_coverage_review` advanced the stage to
`plan_complete` but also auto-created five lexical "Close coverage gap" stubs
(`CG-0MW2KGNZ9001EA9B`, `CG-0MW2KGOET006AARR`, `CG-0MW2KGOUV006U4ZU`,

**Plan: changelog (2026-11-04, plan skill, session
`herdr-1793823012-2636769-3809`).**

# Bind the canonical pre-push full-suite gate to the pushed commit (`--gate-commit`)

## Problem statement

The canonical pre-push hook template (`PRE_PUSH_HOOK_CONTENT` in the
`worklog` package) runs the dev/main full-suite gate as
`run_tests.py --scope full --strict-git-env` with **no commit binding**, so
the gate's verdict describes whichever tree the hook happened to run in. The
implement skill documents the dev-push gate as being bound to the pushed
commit (`run_tests.py --gate-commit <sha> --project-root <root>`) and
SorraAgents' own committed hook implements that; the distributed template
under-delivers on the documented contract, so "the dev push succeeded" does
not currently guarantee the suite ran against the commit that landed.

## Users

- **Framework maintainers** who rely on the dev push as the integration gate:
  "As a maintainer I want a green dev push to mean the full suite ran against
  the commit that landed, not against a dirty working tree."
- **Agent producers** using `implement.py finish` (push from the linked
  worktree): "As a producer I want the gate to validate exactly the worktree
  commit I am pushing, so a stale or dirty main checkout can never produce a
  misleading verdict."
- **Auditors** consuming the per-repo test cache (audit skill F3): "As an
  auditor I want the push's green `scope: full` entry to be keyed to the
  pushed commit's state, so execution-dependent ACs are auto-verified instead
  of re-executed."
- **Repo owners adopting the template via `wl init` / `wl doctor upgrade`**:
  "As a repo owner I want the upgraded hook to keep working with the runner I
  actually have installed, and to fail with an actionable message rather than
  an argparse error."

## Acceptance Criteria

1. `PRE_PUSH_HOOK_CONTENT` captures the pushed `<local_sha>` for each gated
   ref (`refs/heads/dev`, `refs/heads/main`) while still reading pre-push
   stdin **once**, and invokes the resolved runner as
   `--scope full --strict-git-env --json --project-root <repo_root>
   --gate-commit <sha>`. Portable runner resolution is preserved: repo-local
   `skill/test/scripts/run_tests.py` first, then
   `$HOME/.pi/agent/skills/test/scripts/run_tests.py`; neither present
   remains a hard fail (never a silent skip).
2. A push carrying **several different** dev/main commits is refused with an
   actionable message (each `ref=sha` listed, plus recovery: one commit per
   push, `TEST_SCOPE_SKIP=1` / `--no-verify` escape hatches) instead of an
   undefined verdict. Deletion pushes (all-zero sha) are not treated as a
   gated commit.
3. After a green gate, the cache mirror uses the checkout the gate **actually
   resolved** (the runner's `run_tests: gate-root` stderr provenance), not
   merely the push cwd, so the entry lands in the main checkout's
   `.worklog/cache` for the commit that was validated.
4. Behavioural tests pin the behaviour in ContextHub: the stub runner observes
   `--gate-commit <pushed sha>` and `--project-root` for a dev/main push, no
   `--gate-commit` for non-gated refs, the multi-commit refusal blocks the
   push, and the mirror copies from the gate-resolved root. The committed
   `.githooks/pre-push` byte-matches the template (`wl doctor upgrade
   --dry-run --json` reports `pending: []`, every hook `up-to-date`).
5. The dirty-checkout impact is assessed and documented **before** adoption:
   the gate refuses when no clean checkout holds the pushed commit; `.gitignore`d
   `.worklog/` churn does not make a checkout dirty, so the normal
   `implement.py finish` worktree push and a clean main-checkout push still
   resolve in place. The implement skill, `../ContextHub/docs/migrations.md`
   and `docs/DEVELOPER.md` describe the final behaviour and the refusal.
6. All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code
   comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.
7. Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Constraints

- The change lands **upstream** in the `worklog` package (ContextHub
  `PRE_PUSH_HOOK_CONTENT` + committed `.githooks/pre-push`), not as a
  repo-local patch here — the parent item's invariant (no consolidated
  divergence from the canonical template).
- The committed `.githooks/pre-push` must **byte-match** the template, or
  `wl doctor upgrade` reports the hook `outdated` and the "all hooks
  up-to-date" invariant fails.
- The hook stays POSIX `#!/bin/sh`, no bashisms, no `jq`, no new external
  binaries; pre-push stdin is read exactly once (a second read sees EOF).
- `GATE_ROOT_PREFIX` / `GATE_SUBJECT_PREFIX` line formats in `run_tests.py`
  are a contract with the hook — parse `run_tests: gate-root <path>` verbatim
  (paths may contain spaces).
- Fail closed: a missing runner or an unverifiable commit must block the
  push, never pass it.
- Portable runner resolution must be kept — this is precisely why adopting
  SorraAgents' hook wholesale was rejected in CG-0MW1ZBKP0006U1YU.
- When the resolved runner does not support `--gate-commit`, the hook refuses
  with an explicit pre-check message naming the upgrade — never an argparse
  error (producer decision Q1 = (c), below).
- Sequence after the mirroring restoration (CG-0MW1ZBKP0006U1YU /
  WL-0MW20XXWE00466FP): this item edits the same gate block and depends on
  `mirror_suite_cache` existing.

## Existing state

- `../ContextHub/src/doctor/hook-upgrade.ts` → `PRE_PUSH_HOOK_CONTENT` is the
  canonical v3 template (155 lines). Its full-suite gate resolves
  `test_repo_root` / `test_runner` and runs `--scope full --strict-git-env`;
  no `<local_sha>` capture, no `--gate-commit`, no `--project-root`, and the
  cache mirror (added by the parent item) has no gate-root to mirror from.
- `../ContextHub/.githooks/pre-push` is byte-compared against that template by
  `tests/doctor-hook-upgrade.test.ts`; `generateCanonicalHookContent()` is the
  same constant.
- `../SorraAgents/.githooks/pre-push` (270 lines) is the reference
  implementation of the newer contract: `need_full_suite`, `gated_ref_shas`,
  the multi-commit refusal, `--scope full --strict-git-env --json
  --project-root "$repo_root" --gate-commit "$gate_commit"`, stderr captured
  to `gate_err`, `grep '^run_tests: gate-'` echoed to the pusher, and
  `mirror_suite_cache "${gate_root:-$repo_root}"` after a green run.
- `~/.pi/agent/skills/test/scripts/run_tests.py` (and SorraAgents' repo-local
  copy) implement `--gate-commit` / `--project-root`
  (SA-0MVTRBT50005DUEH): `resolve_gate_subject()` returns the push cwd when
  `HEAD` is the pushed commit **and** the checkout is clean, else a clean
  `git worktree list` checkout holding it, else `GateSubjectError` (refuse,
  exit 2) naming the commit and the `TEST_SCOPE_SKIP=1` escape hatch;
  `run_tests: gate-subject` / `gate-root` / `gate-verdict` / `gate-refused`
  lines go to stderr.
- Cleanliness is `git status --untracked-files=all` (via
  `test_cache.is_worktree_clean`); `.worklog/` is gitignored in TCE, so
  worklog churn does not dirty a checkout.
- Tests: `../ContextHub/tests/pre-push-hook-gate.test.ts` runs the committed
  hook in a throwaway git repo with a stubbed `run_tests.py` that records
  `sys.argv[1:]` into `STUB_TEST_LOG`; TCE's

  from a linked worktree with a stubbed runner.

  install, so `--gate-commit` support arrives with the installed runner.

Propagate the newer gate block into the canonical template with the smallest
diff that satisfies the ACs: capture gated `ref=sha` pairs while reading stdin
once, refuse multi-commit pushes with an actionable message, run the gate with
`--gate-commit` + `--project-root` (keeping portable runner resolution and the
hard-fail when absent), surface the runner's `run_tests: gate-*` provenance,
and mirror the cache from the resolved `gate-root` after a green run. Then
update ContextHub's committed hook byte-for-byte, extend the behavioural
tests, and document the final behaviour (implement skill,
`../ContextHub/docs/migrations.md`, `docs/DEVELOPER.md`).

- `../ContextHub/docs/migrations.md` — document the pre-push behaviour change

- `../SorraAgents/skill/implement/SKILL.md` — restate the gate contract as

- **Risk — mirror regression.** Giving `mirror_suite_cache` the push cwd while

Portable runner resolution is preserved: repo-local `skill/test/scripts/run_tests.py` first, then `$HOME/.pi/agent/skills/test/scripts/run_tests.py`; neither present remains a hard fail (never a silent skip).
2. After a green gate, the cache mirror uses the checkout the gate **actually resolved** (the runner's `run_tests: gate-root` stderr provenance), not merely the push cwd, so the entry lands in the main checkout's `.worklog/cache` for the commit that was validated.

# Adopt commit-bound template in TCE and verify a dev push

## Goal

Roll the upgraded canonical pre-push template into TCE's committed hooks and
prove, end to end, that a dev push is gated against the pushed commit and that
the green full-suite cache entry lands in the main checkout for that commit.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. The **installed** `wl` emits the upgraded `PRE_PUSH_HOOK_CONTENT`: the packaged template (`$(dirname "$(readlink -f "$(command -v wl)")")/doctor/hook-upgrade.js`) carries the `worklog:pre-push-hook:v3` marker and the `--gate-commit` block, so the hook TCE adopts is the commit-bound one. The installer mechanism that refreshes the globally resolved `wl` (`scripts/install_pi.sh` in the framework repo) is a framework-repo concern tracked upstream as `SA-0MW2QAEQ0005MTYN` (producer decision Q2 = (a)); this child verifies the TCE-observable outcome, not the installer's internals.
2. `wl doctor upgrade --confirm` in TCE regenerates `.githooks/pre-push`; a follow-up `wl doctor upgrade --dry-run --json` reports `pending: []` with every hook `up-to-date`, and the committed hook byte-matches the template (also reachable through the `scripts/game-repo-scaffold.ts` copy path used by game-repo scaffolding).
3. A dev push from a linked worktree resolves the gate to the pushed commit: the provenance shows `run_tests: gate-subject <sha>` and `run_tests: gate-root <clean checkout>`, the green `scope: full` entry is mirrored into the main checkout's `.worklog/cache`, and `run_tests.py --summary --suite all --json` reports that entry (not `missing`) for the pushed commit.
4. At least one refusal path is exercised and recorded: a multi-commit dev/main push (or a push whose commit no clean checkout holds) is refused with the actionable message and the remote ref stays unadvanced.
5. The sequencing precondition is confirmed: `mirror_suite_cache` exists in the template before the gate block is repointed to the gate-resolved root (parent dependency `CG-0MW1ZBKP0006U1YU` / upstream `WL-0MW20XXWE00466FP`); any residual TCE tracking gap on the parent is recorded as a comment rather than silently skipped.
6. The item records the verification output (gate provenance lines, cache summary, `wl doctor` output).
7. Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Minimal implementation

- Confirm the installed template (`<installed wl>/dist/doctor/hook-upgrade.js`)
  carries the `worklog:pre-push-hook:v3` marker and the `--gate-commit` block;
  refresh the install from the framework repo when it predates them (the
  installer's own gap is `SA-0MW2QAEQ0005MTYN`).
- `wl doctor upgrade --confirm` in TCE; commit the regenerated
  `.githooks/pre-push`; re-run `--dry-run --json` to prove `pending: []`.
- Do a real dev push from a linked worktree (or an `implement.py finish` run)
  and capture the gate provenance, then `run_tests.py --summary --suite all
  --json` to prove the mirrored cache entry.
- Exercise one refusal (multi-commit push from a scratch clone) and capture the
  message; leave the remote unchanged.
- Record outputs as a work-item comment.

## Dependencies

- Consumer test child `CG-0MW2HGXHN003BR6J` (tests authored first, red until
  this child lands).
- `WL-0MW2A3NAP0088IE9` (ContextHub template + committed hook).
- `CG-0MW1ZBKP0006U1YU` (mirroring restoration, sequencing precondition).

## Key Files

- `.githooks/pre-push` (regenerated; byte-match with the template)
- `scripts/game-repo-scaffold.ts` (hooks copy path — verify, no behaviour change)
- `.worklog/cache/` (mirrored full-suite entry verification)

# Intake Brief: Export Session debug tool downloads nothing when the scene names its recorder differently — CG-0MW3KV4D7004KCF0

**Priority: High** | **Type: Bug** | **Stage: intake_complete** | **Open questions: 0 (3 resolved by producer, 2026-11-05)**

> The dev-mode **Export Session** debug tool finds a transcript only when the active scene happens to expose it as `recorder`; any game that names the field differently (The Rising uses `transcriptRecorder`) gets a silently empty `{ turns: [], events: [], metadata }` file. Make recorder discovery name-agnostic across the engine's documented scene shapes and replace the silent empty-file fallback with a visible reason.

**Original request (verbatim, tce-the-rising RISE-0MW2RJ1IV0078G0B "Enable Export"):** *"Currently the export session option in settings debug menu does not export any of the session data."*

## Problem Statement

`createSessionExportTool()` (`src/ui/debug/SessionExportTool.ts`) resolves the session transcript by reading a **single** scene property name, `scene.recorder`. The engine documents the tool as generic ("works in any game scene that has a transcript recorder"), but the field name is a per-game choice: the Gym's transcript scene uses `recorder`, while `tce-the-rising`'s scene exposes `public transcriptRecorder` (`src/scenes/TheRisingScene.ts:139`). When the lookup misses, the tool silently downloads an empty stub (`{ turns: [], events: [], metadata: { exportedAt } }`) — so the developer gets a file that looks like a successful export but contains none of the session data, with no indication that discovery failed. This is a data-free, silent failure in a debugging tool whose only job is to surface data.

The engine already has the multi-name precedent: `StateInspectorOverlay.extractState()` probes `state`, `gameState`, `session` and `recorder` rather than one fixed name (`src/ui/debug/StateInspectorOverlay.ts:52-80`). `SessionExportTool` did not follow it.

## Users

- **Engine / game developer debugging a session (primary)** — wants the exported file to contain the transcript they just played.
  - *"As a developer, I want Export Session to download the real transcript of the active session, so I can analyse or replay a run without finishing the game or using CLI tooling."*
  - *"As a developer whose game names its recorder field something other than `recorder`, I want the tool to find my recorder anyway, so I do not have to rename engine-facing fields to satisfy a debug tool."*
- **Game-scene author (secondary)** — wants to know what the tool expects.
  - *"As a scene author, when there is no transcript to export yet, I want the tool to tell me why nothing was downloaded, instead of handing me an empty file."*

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **Name-agnostic recorder discovery.** The tool resolves the active scene's transcript recorder from the engine's common scene shapes — `recorder`, `transcriptRecorder` and `transcript` — accepting only objects that expose a callable `getTranscript()` (mirroring `StateInspectorOverlay.extractState`'s multi-name probing). A scene shaped like `tce-the-rising`'s `TheRisingScene` (recorder under `transcriptRecorder`, no `recorder` property) exports its full transcript; a scene with no conforming recorder is treated as having no transcript.
2. **Successful export is unchanged and lossless.** When a recorder is found, the downloaded file is `getTranscript()` serialised with `JSON.stringify(..., null, 2)`, named `session-export-<timestamp>.json` with MIME type `application/json` (today's filename/format). The exported JSON equals the recorder's `getTranscript()` output (no truncation, no field stripping).
3. **No silent empty file.** When no conforming recorder is found, or `getTranscript()` throws, **no download is triggered** and a visible reason is surfaced in the Settings panel (the tool's live `description`, re-resolved by the existing 500 ms `DEBUG_DESCRIPTION_POLL_MS` poll) naming the failure — e.g. "No transcript recorder found on this scene". The status reflects only the most recent attempt: a subsequent successful export clears/replaces it. This supersedes the original feature's empty-`turns`-array fallback (CG-0MS1QC3RR004J4Y5, AC "If no transcript is available yet … produces a valid JSON file with an empty turns array"), which is the behaviour being reported as broken.
4. **Pure logic is unit-tested; DOM behaviour is browser-tested.** Discovery, serialisation and the no-recorder/throwing-recorder outcomes are extracted into a Phaser-free module and covered by unit tests (node `unit` project) for: each supported property name, a recorder-like object without `getTranscript`, a non-object property, the no-recorder path, a throwing `getTranscript`, and the serialised payload content. The download-and-feedback path is covered by a browser test (`tests/ui/debug/SessionExportTool.browser.test.ts`, `browser` project) asserting that a real recorder yields exactly one download containing the transcript, and that the no-recorder case yields **no** download plus the visible reason. No existing test regresses.
5. **Build and suites pass.** `npm run build` succeeds and the full project test suite passes with the new changes.
6. **Documentation updated** to reflect the changes, including code comments/JSDoc, `docs/DEVELOPER.md` (§ Debug Tools → Export Session and the debug-tools key-files table), and any relevant wiki or docs site entries: supported recorder property names plus the new no-data behaviour must be stated where the tool is documented.

## Constraints

- **Engine-side, generic, single source.** The fix lands in the core debug tool (`src/ui/debug/`), so every game composing the engine inherits it — no per-game copy, no game-side alias property required.
- **Public surface unchanged.** `createSessionExportTool()` keeps its signature (games import it directly and via `CardGameScene.initSettingsPanel()`'s default list); the `DebugToolsEntry` contract is untouched.
- **Dev-mode only.** The tool stays registered only behind `import.meta.env.DEV`; production tree-shaking must be unaffected (verify the documented `grep` check still returns no debug strings from `dist/`).
- **No new runtime dependencies**, and no change to the other debug tools (the State Inspector has the same single-name limitation — see Risks → scope creep).
- **Cross-repo boundary:** `tce-the-rising` consumes this code through its `./core` submodule; `npm run dev` already syncs the engine `dev` tip (RISE-0MW19AROF0035FRH), so the game picks the fix up without a game-repo code change. The game-repo item that raised this (RISE-0MW2RJ1IV0078G0B) was deleted by the producer at the producer's instruction; all of its evidence is recorded here.
- **Verification commands (copy-paste ready):** `npm run build`; `npx vitest run --project unit tests/ui/debug/`; `npx vitest run --project browser tests/ui/debug/SessionExportTool.browser.test.ts`.
- **Out of scope:** aligning the State Inspector's scene probing; a production (non-dev) export entry; multi-file or bundle exports (state + event log + transcript); CLI/replay parity; renaming any game's recorder field.

## Existing State

- `src/ui/debug/SessionExportTool.ts` (65 lines) — `activate(scene)` does `const recorder = (scene as Record<string, unknown>).recorder;`; if that is an object with a `getTranscript` function it serialises `transcript(), null, 2`, otherwise it serialises the empty stub `{ turns: [], events: [], metadata: { exportedAt } }`. It then builds a `Blob`, an object URL and a synthetic `<a download>` click, and revokes the URL. There is an inline comment noting the pretty-print could adopt `stringifyPayloadSafe()` from `./formatEventLog` for cycle-safe serialisation (deliberately left out of scope in CG-0MVTTR0OC006PWDK).
- `src/ui/CardGameScene.ts:318-323` — the default dev-only debug tools list: `createSessionExportTool(), createStateInspectorTool(), createGameEventLogTool(), createAiDecisionViewerTool()`. Games may pass their own list, which replaces these defaults (The Rising does: `src/scenes/debug/revealAdversaryTool.ts` in `tce-the-rising`).
- `src/ui/SettingsPanel.ts:829-890` — renders the Debug Tools section, calls `tool.activate(this.scene)` on label click (line 864), and re-resolves function-valued `description`s every `DEBUG_DESCRIPTION_POLL_MS = 500` (lines 151, 1194-1222).
- `src/ui/debug/StateInspectorOverlay.ts:52-80` — `extractState()` probes `state`, `gameState`, `session`, `recorder` (only using `recorder` when it has `getTranscript`), then falls back to dumping scene properties. This is the multi-name precedent the export tool is missing.
- `src/ui/debug/formatEventLog.ts` — exports `stringifyPayloadSafe()` (cycle-safe pretty JSON) and `EventLogEntry`; available if the implementer wants cycle-safe serialisation without new code.
- `tce-the-rising` (`src/scenes/TheRisingScene.ts:138-141`): `public transcriptRecorder!: TheRisingTranscriptRecorder;` and `public transcriptStore!: TranscriptStore;` — no `recorder` property, so the export always takes the empty-stub path. `TheRisingTranscriptRecorder extends TranscriptRecorderBase<TheRisingTranscript>` and therefore has `getTranscript()`.
- `core/example-games/gym/scenes/GymTranscriptScene.ts:208` — `private recorder: BlackjackRecorder | null = null;`: the Gym happens to match the current hard-coded name, which is why the bug went unnoticed.
- Test coverage today: **none**. `tests/ui/debug/` contains `AiDecisionOverlay.test.ts`, `GameEventLogOverlay.browser.test.ts` and `formatEventLog.test.ts`; no test references `SessionExportTool` in either the engine or the game repo.
- `docs/DEVELOPER.md:5171-5180` documents the tool as using "a `recorder` with a `getTranscript()` method … Otherwise, it produces an empty transcript with metadata"; `docs/DEVELOPER.md:5455` lists the file in the debug-tools key-files table.

## Desired Change

1. **Extract a pure, Phaser-free resolver** (new module, e.g. `src/ui/debug/transcriptExport.ts`) that, given a scene-like record, returns either the transcript (`{ ok: true, transcript }`) or a reason (`{ ok: false, reason }`): probe `recorder`, `transcriptRecorder`, `transcript` in that order, accept only objects with a callable `getTranscript`, call it defensively (a throw becomes a reasoned failure), and serialise with `JSON.stringify(..., null, 2)`.
2. **Rewire `SessionExportTool`** to use the resolver: on success download exactly as today (same filename pattern, MIME type, anchor-click mechanism); on failure trigger no download, record the reason in module-scoped state, and expose it through the entry's function-valued `description` so the open Settings panel shows it within one poll interval. Reset/refresh that status on a later successful export.
3. **Tests:** unit tests for the resolver and serialisation (node project) and a browser test for the download/no-download behaviour and the visible description change.
4. **Docs:** update `docs/DEVELOPER.md` (Export Session function description: supported property names, lossless payload, no-data behaviour) and the module JSDoc, keeping the production-tree-shaking note accurate.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `src/ui/debug/transcriptExport.ts` — **New**: pure resolver/serialiser (scene-record → transcript or reason), node-safe (no Phaser import).
- `src/ui/debug/SessionExportTool.ts` — Use the resolver; download on success; on failure set the module-scoped reason surfaced via a function-valued `description`; update JSDoc.
- `src/ui/debug/index.ts` — Re-export the resolver if it belongs on the debug-tools surface (barrel).
- `tests/ui/debug/transcriptExport.test.ts` — **New**: unit coverage for all supported names, non-conforming objects, throwing `getTranscript`, no-recorder reason, and payload serialisation.
- `tests/ui/debug/SessionExportTool.browser.test.ts` — **New**: browser coverage for the download (one file, correct content/name) and the no-download + visible-reason path.
- `docs/DEVELOPER.md` — § Debug Tools → Export Session function/behaviour bullets; key-files table row if the new module is listed.
- `tce-the-rising/src/scenes/TheRisingScene.ts` — **read-only evidence** for the naming mismatch; no change required.

## Risks & Assumptions

### Risks

- **Heuristic names can still miss a third naming.** Probing three names does not make discovery universal (a scene could use `transcriptLog`). *Mitigation:* document the supported names in `docs/DEVELOPER.md` and the module JSDoc, and report the miss visibly (AC3) instead of silently exporting nothing — a visible reason is enough for a developer to rename or extend the list. An explicit per-game accessor (e.g. an optional `getTranscript` hook on the tool factory) is a deliberately deferred option, not part of this item.
- **Feedback placement.** The reason must be visible while the Settings panel is open (the click happens inside it). The plan avoids z-order risk by reusing the panel's existing live-description rendering rather than adding a world-space toast beneath the panel; if a toast is preferred later, its depth relative to `DEPTH_PANEL_BG`/`DEPTH_PANEL_CONTENT` must be handled.
- **Test environment split.** The unit project runs `environment: 'node'`, so `Blob`/`document`/`URL` code cannot be unit-tested headlessly; download assertions belong in the `browser` project (`*.browser.test.ts`), with the pure logic in the unit project. Trying to fake the DOM in node would test the fake, not the tool.
- **Stale feedback text.** A failure reason surfaced through the live description persists until the next attempt, so a later success must clear it (and a later failure must replace it) or the panel shows a misleading status. *Mitigation:* AC2/AC3 require the status to reflect only the most recent attempt, and the browser test asserts both directions.
- **Behaviour change for existing consumers.** Removing the empty-file fallback changes today's output for scenes without a recorder (previously a valid empty JSON file). *Mitigation:* the empty file is the reported defect; AC3 documents the replacement and AC6 requires it in the docs.
- **Scope creep.** The State Inspector has the same single-name assumption (it misses `risingState`/`transcriptRecorder`), and a production-facing export, multi-file bundles (state + events) or a CLI parity change are all tempting. All are recorded as separate opportunities, not added here.

### Assumptions

- Transcripts are plain, JSON-serialisable data (The Rising's `TheRisingTranscript` is a structural interface of plain fields; verified in `tce-the-rising/src/TheRisingTranscript.ts`), so a plain `JSON.stringify` is lossless here; cycle-safe serialisation via `stringifyPayloadSafe()` remains optional hardening, not a requirement.
- Scene properties are readable as plain own properties (`public` fields, as in `TheRisingScene.transcriptRecorder` and `GymTranscriptScene.recorder`); no accessor protocol is introduced.
- Games reach this code through the `./core` submodule, so an engine fix is sufficient for `tce-the-rising`; no game-repo code change or alias property is needed.
- The tool stays dev-only; there is no production user-facing export requirement.

## Related Work

- **Session export in Debug section (CG-0MS1QC3RR004J4Y5)** [completed, feature]: introduced `src/ui/debug/SessionExportTool.ts`, its registration in `CardGameScene.initSettingsPanel()`, and the (then intended) generic transcript download. Its AC "works in any game scene that has a transcript recorder" is exactly what this bug violates; its empty-`turns`-array fallback is what AC3 replaces.
- **Detect when running in developer mode and provide debug tools (CG-0MQZYFG3C0063DN3)** [completed]: parent of the above; established `isDevMode()` gating and the Debug Tools section.
- **Game Event Log debug tool (CG-0MS1QC3KR004C7UQ)** / **Pretty-print game events (CG-0MVTTR0OC006PWDK)** [completed]: sibling debug tool; introduced `src/ui/debug/formatEventLog.ts` with `stringifyPayloadSafe()` and left the session-export serialiser deliberately unchanged (its inline note places cycle-safe serialisation out of that item's scope). Optional reuse here.
- **State inspector overlay with filter (CG-0MS1QC3E1003G5S4)** [completed]: sibling debug tool whose `extractState()` already probes multiple scene property names — the pattern this fix adopts.
- **Documentation update for dev mode debug tools (CG-0MS1QBONV0082TIQ)** [completed]: owns the `docs/DEVELOPER.md` Debug Tools section AC6 updates.
- **In-Game Transcript Export Button (CG-0MLTFRU211Y0Z2WU)** [completed, feature]: added the in-game transcript download button and the `Blob` + `URL.createObjectURL` + anchor-click download pattern this tool reuses; its "empty transcript still exports" rule is another instance of the empty-file behaviour AC3 replaces in the debug tool.
- **AI Decision Viewer debug tool (CG-0MS1QC4SC006FPFM)** [completed]: sibling debug entry that resolves its data from a global singleton rather than a scene property, the alternative access pattern this fix deliberately does not adopt (the transcript recorder genuinely lives on the scene).
- **Update Core on npm run dev (RISE-0MW19AROF0035FRH, tce-the-rising)** [completed]: makes game `npm run dev` sync the engine `dev` tip, which is how this fix reaches the reporting game.

## Appendix: Clarifying Questions & Answers

- **Q1 (where the fix lives, resolved — supersedes the RISE item).** Q: "Where should the fix live? **(A)** *Recommended* — engine-side: `SessionExportTool` detects common recorder names (`recorder`, `transcriptRecorder`, `transcript`) mirroring `StateInspectorOverlay`, with engine tests; the game needs only a regression test, and this requires an engine work item plus submodule bump; (B) game-side only: add a `recorder` getter alias on `TheRisingScene`; (C) both." — Answer (producer, 2026-11-05): **"Create a work item in the engine and delete this one."** i.e. **(A) engine-side**, with the engine item being this one (CG-0MW3KV4D7004KCF0) and the reporting game item RISE-0MW2RJ1IV0078G0B deleted. Source: interactive reply to the intake interview. Evidence: `src/ui/debug/SessionExportTool.ts:32-46` (single-name lookup + empty-stub fallback), `src/ui/debug/CardGameScene.ts:318-323` (default registration), `tce-the-rising/src/scenes/TheRisingScene.ts:139` (`transcriptRecorder`), `core/example-games/gym/scenes/GymTranscriptScene.ts:208` (`recorder`).
- **Q2 (export payload, resolved).** Q: "What should the export contain? **(A)** *Recommended* — the transcript JSON only; (B) transcript plus live runtime state and the buffered game events as one bundle; (C) transcript wrapped in an export envelope with app/version/debug marker." — Answer (producer, 2026-11-05): **(A) — transcript JSON only.** Source: interactive reply to the intake interview. **Recommended and accepted:** (A) keeps the payload replay-parseable and matches the documented tool behaviour (`docs/DEVELOPER.md:5171-5180`); anything richer becomes a separate item.
- **Q3 (no-recorder behaviour, resolved).** Q: "What should happen when no recorder/transcript is available (e.g. before a session starts)? **(A)** keep today's silent empty-file download; **(B)** *Recommended* — do not download; show a visible message naming the reason (and still download when data exists); (C) download with an embedded error/reason field." — Answer (producer, 2026-11-05): **(B) — no download, visible reason.** Source: interactive reply to the intake interview. **Recommended and accepted:** (B) — the silent empty file is what made this defect hard to diagnose, and a visible reason is testable.
- **Q: "Is the job only the download path, or also the recorder discovery?"** — Answer: both, but the failure is discovery-time (`scene.recorder` misses `transcriptRecorder`), so discovery is the fix and the download mechanism (Blob + anchor click) stays as-is. Evidence: `src/ui/debug/SessionExportTool.ts` (lookup at lines 32-46, download at 51-61). Source: repo inspection.
- **Q: "Does the Gym legitimately export today?"** — Answer: yes — `GymTranscriptScene` stores its recorder as `recorder`, matching the hard-coded name, which is why the tool appeared to work. Evidence: `core/example-games/gym/scenes/GymTranscriptScene.ts:208,331`. Source: repo inspection.
- **Q: "Is there already a multi-name scene helper to reuse?"** — Answer: no shared helper; `StateInspectorOverlay.extractState()` inlines its own multi-name probing, so this item extracts the export-side equivalent rather than sharing the inspector's inline code. Evidence: `src/ui/debug/StateInspectorOverlay.ts:52-80`. Source: repo inspection, `grep` over `src/ui/debug/`.
- **Q: "Are there existing tests for the tool?"** — Answer: none in either repo. Evidence: `tests/ui/debug/` listing; `grep -rn 'SessionExportTool' tests` returns nothing. Source: repo inspection.

# Filter core-only `scaffold:game`/`scaffold:games` out of generated game repos

**Cross-repo delivery counterpart of** `MS-0MVSBGYMD009CP7D` (tce-main-street) — _Deliver core template change to Tableau-Card-Engine (parent AC3)_ — and of `MS-0MVO30VXS002A1Z0` (its parent, the discovery item).

## Why this item exists

Every generated game repo (`tce-main-street`, `tce-golf`, `tce-blackjack`, …) declared
`scaffold:game` and `scaffold:games` pointing at `tsx scripts/game-repo-scaffold.ts` — a file
that exists only in the core (Option C: a game repo has no root `scripts/` tree). Invoking
either script failed with module-not-found.

Root cause: `renderPackageJson` in `scripts/game-repo-scaffold.ts` inherited the core's whole
`scripts` map, so the core's own `scaffold:game` / `scaffold:games` entries leaked into every
generated repo.

## The change (authored, tracked here for landing on the engine's `dev`)

- `scripts/game-repo-scaffold.ts`: an explicitly named `CORE_ONLY_SCRIPTS` drop-list filters
  both keys out of the inherited scripts map, with the Option C rationale inline and the wider
  class of core-only scripts left to a follow-up.
- `tests/scripts/game-repo-scaffold.test.ts`: the `MANIFEST` fixture declares both keys and a
  new test asserts the rendered `package.json` omits them while other inherited scripts
  (e.g. `save-load-smoke`) and the game-repo `scaffold` entry point still pass through.

Both land in one commit (test-first: the test asserts absence, so the engine's dev-push gate
would refuse the test without the filter).

# test-failure: context-budget thresholds guard fails — committed thresholds missing `skill_implement_md`

## Problem statement

`dev` HEAD fails its own full-suite pre-push gate: the committed
`docs/dev/context-budget.thresholds.json` predates the `skill_implement_md`
component that the installed `context-audit` `measure_context.py` now emits from
`--generate-thresholds`, so
`tests/scripts/context-budget-thresholds.test.ts > committed thresholds match
the measured startup context surface` fails with an exact-match diff. Because the
guard runs inside the `unit` profile, **every** push to `dev` is blocked —
including docs-only work unrelated to the context budget (CG-0MW917K7V009LMLE
had to be pushed with `TEST_SCOPE_SKIP=1`).

## Users and user stories

- **Engine maintainer** — *As a maintainer, I want to push unrelated work to
  `dev` without a stale thresholds file turning the whole tree red, so that the
  fast unit gate stays a useful signal.*
- **Agent pushing to `dev`** — *As an agent, I want `npm run context:refresh` to
  name **every** measured component, so that a tool-side component addition like
  `skill_implement_md` shows up in the refresh delta instead of drifting
  silently.*
- **Newcomer reading the gate docs** — *As a newcomer, I want
  `docs/dev/context-budget.md` to list every key in the thresholds file, so I can
  tell which components are part of the startup `total` and which are separate
  gates.*

## Acceptance Criteria

- `docs/dev/context-budget.thresholds.json` contains the **full** measured
  component set, including `skill_implement_md` (measured as `0` in this repo —
  the core carries no local `skill/` tree), and its values are **regenerated**
  with `scripts/refresh-context-thresholds.sh`, never hand-edited.
- `bash scripts/refresh-context-thresholds.sh --check` exits `0` on the fixed
  tree, and the guard test
  `tests/scripts/context-budget-thresholds.test.ts` passes in the `unit` profile
  (both cases: the exact-match check and the `--check`-reports-STALE helper case).
- `scripts/refresh-context-thresholds.sh` reports every component present in the
  measured thresholds JSON instead of the hardcoded four-key `order` list, so a
  future component added by `measure_context.py` appears in the printed
  before/after/delta table (and an unknown/extra key is shown rather than
  silently dropped).
- `docs/dev/context-budget.md` documents the full component set — adding
  `skill_implement_md` to the component table with a note that it is a separate
  gate and **not** part of `total` — and the example thresholds JSON in that page
  matches the committed file's key set. Any component list in
  `docs/DEVELOPER.md`'s context-budget section is consistent with it.
- A test asserts the refresh helper's printed output names every component in the
  measured map (so the drift-proofing in AC 3 cannot regress), without weakening
  the existing fail-open behaviour (no `python3` or no `context-audit` skill ⇒
  skip with a clear reason).
- All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code
  comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.
- Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Impact

Agents and maintainers get a green `dev` tree again — any push that does not grow
the startup context surface goes straight through — and the refresh helper names
every measured component, so this drift class cannot recur silently.

## Constraints

- **Exact-match convention.** TCE threshold values equal the measured byte counts
  exactly; the fix is a regenerate-and-commit, not a tolerance bump.
- **Fail-open preserved.** The guard test must keep skipping (with a reason) when
  `python3` or `context-audit` is absent; do not convert it to a hard failure.
- **Do not tighten the pre-push hook.** `.githooks/pre-push` consumes the file in
  `--thresholds` *comparison* mode, which tolerates a missing key. Scaffolded
  game repos (e.g. `../tce-main-street`) legitimately ship a four-key file for
  their own surface, so making the hook require every key would break them. The
  strict equality requirement belongs to the guard test only.
- **No cross-repo changes are needed for this fix.** Game repos carry no copy of
  the guard test; they receive the refresh script through
  `scripts/game-repo-scaffold.ts`, so the drift-proofing propagates on their next
  scaffold run (no re-scaffold required to unblock `dev`).
- **Single commit.** The thresholds file, script and docs changes must land
  together — a partial push re-reds the gate.
- Out of scope: adding the guard test to game repos; converting `skill_implement_md`
  into a hard pre-push budget; the SorraAgents `skill_implement_md: 20000` budget
  convention (that repo has no guard test and uses max-bytes semantics).

## Existing state

Measured on `dev` @ `a26d4bf0`:

```console
$ python3 ~/.pi/agent/skills/context-audit/scripts/measure_context.py \
    --repo-root "$PWD" --include-hidden --generate-thresholds
{ "global_agents": 0, "project_agents": 67912, "skill_implement_md": 0,
  "skills_prose": 0, "total": 67912 }

$ bash scripts/refresh-context-thresholds.sh --check
STALE: committed thresholds do not match the measured startup context surface.
# exit 1
```

- Committed [`docs/dev/context-budget.thresholds.json`](../../docs/dev/context-budget.thresholds.json)
  holds only `global_agents`, `project_agents`, `skills_prose`, `total`
  (`project_agents` / `total` = 67912).
- `measure_context.py` emits five keys; `skill_implement_md` is
  `skill/implement/SKILL.md` body size — `0` here because the **core repo has no
  local `skill/` tree** (`skill/context-audit/` is also absent, so the global
  skill install is resolved first in both the hook and the test).
- `tests/scripts/context-budget-thresholds.test.ts` (guard, unit profile) asserts
  exact equality of committed vs measured, and separately asserts
  `refresh-context-thresholds.sh --check` reports STALE on a throwaway stale repo
  without rewriting it.
- `scripts/refresh-context-thresholds.sh` prints its delta over a hardcoded
  `order = ["global_agents", "project_agents", "skills_prose", "total"]`, which is
  why the new component did not surface when the tool last changed.
- `docs/dev/context-budget.md` documents the same four components and shows a
  four-key example thresholds file.
- `npm run context:refresh` / `npm run context:check` are the documented entry
  points.

## Desired change

1. Regenerate `docs/dev/context-budget.thresholds.json` via
   `scripts/refresh-context-thresholds.sh`, so the file carries all five keys with
   the measured values.
2. Make the refresh script's delta reporter derive its component list from the
   measured/committed JSON (canonical order first, extra keys appended) instead of
   a hardcoded list, and include `skill_implement_md` in its output.
3. Document the fifth component in `docs/dev/context-budget.md` (table + example
   JSON, with the "separate gate, not part of `total`" note) and keep
   `docs/DEVELOPER.md` consistent.
4. Add a regression assertion that the refresh output names every measured
   component, keeping the existing fail-open skip behaviour.

## Key Files

- `docs/dev/context-budget.thresholds.json` — Regenerate: add `skill_implement_md` (value `0`).
- `scripts/refresh-context-thresholds.sh` — Replace the hardcoded `order` list with a derived component list so new measure components are always reported.
- `docs/dev/context-budget.md` — Component table + example thresholds JSON: document `skill_implement_md` as a separate gate outside `total`.
- `tests/scripts/context-budget-thresholds.test.ts` — Existing guard; add a focused assertion that the refresh output names every measured component (preserve fail-open skip).
- `docs/DEVELOPER.md` — Context-budget subsection; align any component enumeration with the corrected docs.
- `scripts/game-repo-scaffold.ts` — Reference only (game repos inherit the refresh script and their own doc note); no change expected unless the docs-descriptor text enumerates components.

## Risks and assumptions

- **Assumption:** `skill_implement_md` is `0` for the engine because the core has
  no `skill/` tree; the value is *measured*, and the guard test measures at the
  same time, so a different environment (e.g. one with a local `skill/` copy) would
  record its own value consistently.
- **Risk — environment-derived values.** The committed numbers come from the
  machine that runs the refresh (the global skill install). Mitigation: the guard
  test is local-only (PR CI is build-only) and fail-open when tooling is absent;
  refresh and test on the same install, as the documented workflow already says.
- **Risk — a naive AC3 change breaks the `--check` path.** The `--check` branch
  builds its own JSON; keep both branches using the same component list and keep
  `--check` non-writing (the guard test asserts the file is untouched).
- **Risk — AC5 assertion is environment-sensitive.** Keep it a structural
  assertion (key names present in output), not a byte-count assertion, so it does
  not re-introduce exact-match fragility.
- **Scope-creep risk.** Tightening the pre-push hook, adding the guard to game
  repos, or turning this into auto-ratcheting thresholds are recorded as follow-up
  candidates, **not** folded into this fix.

## Related work

- **CG-0MW917K7V009LMLE** — *Document Main Street per-upgrade art copies in
  CREDITS.md and fix stale paths* (completed): docs-only push that had to use
  `TEST_SCOPE_SKIP=1` because of this failure.
- **CG-0MUFCL5N50023PHJ** — *AGENTS.md exceeds context-budget threshold, blocking
  all pushes to dev*: introduced the thresholds gate, refresh script and this
  guard test.
- **CG-0MUFAUPI6002P6PE**, **CG-0MTCRF0K2006N0HR** — earlier `AGENTS.md`-growth
  threshold drifts (`46024 > 45898`, `41706 > 41692`); precedent for the
  "drift blocks everyone" class.
- **CG-0MW0KURL8002XOV9**, **CG-0MW0SBXKW000T4C0**, **CG-0MW0SC46S007E6GC**,
  **CG-0MW0SCE8G000TROO** — game-repo scaffold: copies the refresh script, seeds
  each repo's own thresholds and `.githooks/pre-push`.
- Docs: [`docs/dev/context-budget.md`](../../docs/dev/context-budget.md),
  [`docs/DEVELOPER.md`](../../docs/DEVELOPER.md) (context budget),
  [`docs/dev/multi-repo-architecture.md`](../../docs/dev/multi-repo-architecture.md) (gate shipped to game repos),
  `~/.pi/agent/skills/context-audit/scripts/measure_context.py` (component source).

## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items

- **CG-0MUFAUPI6002P6PE** – [infra] context-budget pre-push gate blocks all dev
  pushes: AGENTS.md 46024 B > 45898 B threshold (completed)
- **CG-0MW0SC46S007E6GC** – Scaffold seeds context-budget thresholds (completed)
- **CG-0MTCRF0K2006N0HR** – [infra] context-budget pre-push gate blocks all dev
  pushes: AGENTS.md 41706 B > 41692 B threshold (completed)

### Repository file matches

- `docs/DEVELOPER.md` — context-budget section (component/gate wording)
- `AGENTS.md` — quality-gates wording that references the thresholds file
- `docs/dev/multi-repo-architecture.md` — the gate as shipped to game repos

## Appendix: Clarifying questions and answers

No clarifying questions were required: the seed context (symptom, cause, fix,
impact) plus repository research was sufficient to draft the brief. Findings that
replaced would-be questions:

- Q (research, self-answered): *Which keys does the measured map contain, and is
  `skill_implement_md` non-zero here?* — Answer: five keys; `skill_implement_md`
  is `0` in this repo because it has no local `skill/` tree. Evidence:
  `measure_context.py --generate-thresholds` run on `dev` @ `a26d4bf0`.
- Q (research, self-answered): *Is the strict equality only in the guard test, or
  also in the pre-push hook?* — Answer: strict equality is the guard test's
  exact-match check; `.githooks/pre-push` compares in `--thresholds` mode and
  tolerates missing keys, so scaffolded game repos with four-key files stay green.
  Evidence: `.githooks/pre-push` lines ~94–104; `../tce-main-street/docs/dev/context-budget.thresholds.json`.
- Q (research, self-answered): *Does anything else assert the thresholds key set
  or the refresh delta table?* — Answer: no — only
  `tests/scripts/context-budget-thresholds.test.ts` asserts the file's contents;
  `tests/scripts/game-repo-scaffold.test.ts` only stubs the script. Evidence: repo
  grep for `context-budget.thresholds`.
- Recorded decision (assumption, not a question): the fix includes the AC 3
  drift-proofing and AC 4 docs alignment rather than a bare thresholds refresh,
  because a refresh-only fix leaves the hardcoded four-key reporter in place —
  the mechanism that let this drift go unnoticed. Scope-creep candidates are
  listed under Risks and are explicitly out of scope.

# Objective

Add an **opt-in drag-to-reorder capability to the shared `HandView`** so a player can drag a card left/right *within* the hand row to change its position (C, B, A → A, B, C), with an animated re-layout, card-move SFX, reduced-motion support, and a `cardreorder` event that lets the owning game keep its model order in sync.

## Problem statement

`HandView` supports click-to-select, drag-and-drop onto a *pile* (`targetPileIndex` + validator) and programmatic `sortCards()`, but a card cannot be dragged to a new position **inside the same hand**. Cards are therefore stuck in deal order — even in games where hand order carries no rules meaning, being able to arrange "the card I plan to play next" is a normal tableau affordance. Any game that wants it today must hand-roll bespoke drag logic, which the project's HandView requirement forbids.

## Users

- **Player (Gym demo).** "As a player holding C, B, A, I want to drag A to the front so the hand reads A, B, C, so I can arrange cards in the order I plan to use them."
- **Player in a drag-to-play game (e.g. Gym pile drag).** "I want hand reordering to slot in without breaking the existing drag-to-discard gesture."
- **Game developer.** "I want hand reordering enabled with one option, and a callback so my game model stays authoritative rather than the view quietly owning the order."

## Acceptance Criteria

- `HandView` exposes an opt-in reorder capability (constructor option `reorderEnabled` plus `setReorderEnabled()` / `getReorderEnabled()`), **default off**, so every existing drag-to-pile, cascade-drag and click-to-select behaviour is unchanged when the option is not enabled (existing `HandView` unit and Gym `gym-handpile-*` browser tests keep passing without modification).
- With reorder enabled, dragging a card horizontally within the hand row and releasing it over a different slot reorders the hand: releasing past the left edge of slot 0 inserts at index 0, releasing over the boundary between two cards inserts at that boundary, and releasing on the card's own slot is a no-op (no visual change, no event, no SFX).
- The row is re-laid out with animation on commit (snapped instantly under reduced motion), sprite/z-order/label/tint-overlay/outline alignment follow the new indices, and a card-move SFX (`sfx-card-swap`, which already exists in `public/assets/audio/default`) plays through the injected `SoundManager`; nothing plays when the reorder is a no-op or when no `SoundManager` is wired.
- `HandView` emits a `cardreorder` event carrying `{ from, to }` (and the card) after a committed move, and `getCards()` / `getCardCenters()` reflect the new order, so a scene can reorder its own model array; when the pointer is over a pile/other registered drop target the existing `dragend`/validator path keeps precedence and `HandView` does not reorder.
- The Gym hand/pile scene demonstrates the capability end-to-end — a runtime toggle through the existing SLL-positioned button bar, help-panel text describing what it does and when to use it, and an event-log entry on each reorder — and the contract is documented in `docs/DEVELOPER.md` (Hand & Pile Rendering) and `docs/gym/GYM_INDEX.md`.
- New unit tests cover insertion-index computation (left edge, between cards, right edge, own slot, fixed `maxSlots` capacity template), the committed array/sprite order, the no-op case, the reduced-motion path and the SFX wiring; a browser test drives a real pointer drag in the Gym scene and asserts the hand order changed and the existing drag-to-discard gesture still works.
- All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, `README` if developer-facing commands change, and the relevant docs site entries (`docs/DEVELOPER.md`, `docs/gym/GYM_INDEX.md`, `docs/ui-animations.md` and `docs/ui/ADAPTER-GUIDE.md` where the HandView contract is described).
- Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Impact

Players can drag a card to a new position inside their hand, so a hand can be arranged in the order they plan to play it instead of being frozen in deal order.

## Constraints

- **No regression to existing drag semantics.** Reorder must be a separate opt-in mode; `dragstart` / `dragmove` / `dragend`, `setDragValidator()`, `setDragTargetPileIndex()` and cascade multi-card pickup behave exactly as today when the option is off.
- **Model stays authoritative.** `HandView` is a view: it reports the move (`cardreorder`) and updates its own `cards`/`sprites` order, but the game's own array (`state.hand` in Main Street, the Gym scene's `hand`) is the source of truth and must be reordered by the scene handler, otherwise the next refresh re-renders the old order.
- **Works with custom-rendered hands.** The default sprite path and the `renderCard` / custom-container path (Main Street, Sushi Go style) must both reorder without game-side bespoke drag code; docs must state that custom renderers must not cache index-derived state across a reorder.
- **Layout invariants preserved.** Reordering must respect the fixed capacity template (`maxSlots` / `showPositionOutlines`) without re-centring the row or disturbing outline slots; insertion geometry comes from the existing helpers (`getCardCenters()`, `getBasePosition()`, `_computeRowPositions()`) rather than new hard-coded pixels, and the transient insertion affordance is a plain display object (no `setMask`/`GeometryMask`).
- **SLL for any new UI**, and the Gym toggle reuses the existing button-bar / help-panel pattern (no absolute pixel positioning of new controls).
- **SFX + accessibility conventions.** Reuse the baseline `sfx-card-swap` key (no game-scoped string literals, per `docs/SFX_CONVENTION.md`); honour reduced motion and mute/volume through `SoundManager`.
- **No undo/redo coupling in the engine.** Games that use `UndoRedoManager` decide whether to wrap `cardreorder` in a command; `HandView` does not own undo.
- **Out of scope:** adopting reordering in sibling game repos (Main Street, Coloretto, …) — each is its own repo/worklog item; keyboard/accessible reorder alternative; vertical cascade reorder (see Risks).

## Existing state

- `src/ui/HandView.ts` (≈2,240 lines) already has the pieces a reorder needs: a drag lifecycle with `DRAG_THRESHOLD` and `_boundPointerMove` / `_boundPointerUp`, `_computeDragRange()` (single index horizontal, `[0..index]` in vertical cascade), `_storeOriginalPositions()` / `_animateSnapBack()` / `_animateDragAccept()`, an **animated reorder precedent** in `sortCards()` (`reorderSpritesForNewCardOrder()` + per-sprite tweens to `computeCardPositions()`), the fixed capacity template and outlines (`maxSlots`, `_computeOutlineSlots()`, `_outlineDepth()`), plus geometry helpers `getCardCenters()`, `getBasePosition()` and `getInsertionPosition()`.
- Drag *to a pile* is the only supported drop today: the scene hit-tests piles in `dragmove`, calls `setDragTargetPileIndex()`, and `_boundPointerUp` asks `_dragValidator` and emits `dragend`. Gym wires this in `example-games/gym/scenes/GymHandPileScene.ts` (`dragstart` / `dragmove` / `dragend` handlers, drop-zone highlights, snap-back rebuild).
- Main Street does **not** use `HandView` drag: it registers hand cards as draggables with its own `DragDropManager` (`../tce-main-street/src/scenes/MainStreetRendererStreet.ts`, `MainStreetRendererDragDrop.ts`), so it is unaffected by this change and would need its own adoption item.
- No `moveCard` / `insertCard` / `reorderCards` API exists on `HandView`; `sortCards()` sorts by a comparator only. There is no shared array-move utility in `src/`.
- Gym `GymHandPileScene` already has the `[ Disable Drag ]` toggle, `[ Sort Hand ]` and `[ Shuffle Hand ]` buttons, position-outline toggle and a documented help panel — the natural host for the demo.

## Desired change

1. **`HandView` reorder mode.** New option `reorderEnabled` (default `false`) + `setReorderEnabled()` / `getReorderEnabled()`. While a horizontal-layout drag is in progress, derive an insertion index from the pointer X against the current slot centres; while the pointer stays in the hand row band (and no pile target is active) show an insertion affordance (gap shift preview or a plain insertion marker) and, on release, commit the move.
2. **Commit path.** Splice `cards` from → to, rebuild the `sprites` order with the existing pre-sort mapping technique, re-lay positions with the existing animated path (instant under reduced motion), refresh depth/labels/tints/outlines, play `sfx-card-swap` via an injected `SoundManager`, and emit `cardreorder`.
3. **Public event contract.** `cardreorder` payload `{ from, to, card }` added to `HandViewEvents` (exported from `@ui`), documented as "reorder your own model in the same way; HandView has already reordered its view".
4. **Gym demonstration.** Toggle in the hand/pile scene's existing button bar, event-log entry, updated status label and help text (features / controls / usage example).
5. **Docs.** `docs/DEVELOPER.md` Hand & Pile Rendering section: reorder contract, model-sync responsibility, coexistence with pile drops, custom-renderer caveat. `docs/gym/GYM_INDEX.md`: add the new `HandView` APIs to the Hand & Pile row. `docs/ui-animations.md` / `docs/ui/ADAPTER-GUIDE.md`: the animation + adapter notes.

**Key Files:**

- `src/ui/HandView.ts` — reorder option/API, insertion-index computation, drag-commit path, `cardreorder` event, SFX hook (main change)
- `src/ui/index.ts` — export the new event payload type alongside `HandViewEvents`
- `src/ui/layoutCardPositions.ts` — only if insertion geometry needs a shared helper (avoid duplicating slot maths)
- `example-games/gym/scenes/GymHandPileScene.ts` — demo toggle, status label, help text, event-log entries, `cardreorder` handler reordering the scene's `hand`
- `tests/ui/handView.reorder.test.ts` — new: insertion index (edges, boundaries, own slot, `maxSlots` template), committed order, no-op, reduced motion, SFX, pile-target precedence
- `tests/handView/gym-handpile-reorder.browser.test.ts` — new: real drag gesture reorders; drag-to-discard still works
- `docs/DEVELOPER.md` — Hand & Pile Rendering: reorder contract + model-sync rule
- `docs/gym/GYM_INDEX.md` — Hand & Pile Interactions row: new APIs and test references
- `docs/ui-animations.md` — reorder animation/SFX behaviour
- `docs/ui/ADAPTER-GUIDE.md` — custom `renderCard` hands must tolerate reordering

## Risks and assumptions

- **Gesture conflict with drag-to-play (highest risk).** In a scene where dragging a hand card already means "drop on a pile", an inside-hand release could be ambiguous. *Mitigation:* reorder only when the pointer is inside the hand row band **and** no pile target is reported for that move; the existing `dragend`/validator path always wins; the mode is opt-in; browser tests cover both gestures in the same scene.
- **Model/view divergence.** If a game ignores `cardreorder`, its next `setCards()` refresh silently reverts the hand. *Mitigation:* the event is the documented contract, the Gym demo implements the handler, and the docs state the responsibility explicitly.
- **Capacity template interactions.** `maxSlots` keeps fixed slot positions (CG-0MUAYBB4E007LWEQ), so insertion maths must use slot centres, not "card count re-centring"; overflow hands (more cards than `maxSlots`) need defined insertion behaviour. *Mitigation:* reuse the existing geometry helpers and add explicit `maxSlots` tests (occupied and empty slots, overflow hands).
- **Custom renderers.** Scenes that render containers with their own depth/labels (Main Street, Sushi Go) may key visuals off the index; reordering changes indices. *Mitigation:* document the caveat; HandView reorders only objects it manages; the Gym demo exercises the custom-render path as well as the default sprite path if cheap.
